facts.statement: The researchers used a longitudinal cohort study design involving 837 people who had experienced childhood trauma.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study measured how frontal alpha brain wave connectivity changed over time from adolescence into young adulthood.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Experiencing childhood sexual assault and carrying the APOEε4 gene were both connected to specific patterns in brain connectivity.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Participants who suffered childhood sexual assault showed higher initial brain connectivity but less improvement in three specific brain connections over time.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Carriers of the APOEε4 gene started with lower connectivity in the left frontocentral brain region but showed a steeper increase in connectivity over time.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: In people with the APOEε4 gene, childhood sexual assault was linked to higher starting levels and slower growth in specific frontal brain connections.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The observed brain connectivity patterns were strongly linked to symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder and alcohol use disorder.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The study found no direct connection between carrying the APOEε4 gene and developing PTSD or alcohol use disorder symptoms.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors suggest these results could help identify at-risk groups and guide prevention efforts, though they frame this as a potential application rather than a proven outcome.
facts.subject: humans
